name: Dusty hazel tone
lede: Dusty hazel tone is a dull yellow-green, ColorHub's English name for the Japanese traditional color Koke-iro, literally "moss color."

sections.title: Moss color
sections.body: Koke-iro (苔色) is listed among Japan's traditional colors on Wikipedia, where the kanji are glossed simply as "moss color" [1]. The name describes the color of moss itself rather than a dye or a place [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[warbler-green]], [[spanish-bistre]], [[serpentine-green]] and [[buffy-citrine]], at 3.3, 3.5, 4.2 and 4.4 ΔE [1][3]. 3, 3.5, 4.2 and 4.4 ΔE [3]. A fifth, slightly farther neighbor is [[dull-citrine]], 4.8 ΔE away, duller [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds this color in 868 of 23,781 paintings, about 3.7 percent, as photographed [2]. The earliest match is Simone Martini's *Saint Matthew*, dated to 1315, though the matching area covers only about a quarter of the canvas, a floor and not a first, since the archive's early centuries are thin [2]. The rate is highest in a sample of 416 paintings from the 1770s, where it appears in 38, about two and a half times the archive's overall rate [2]. Among sampled painters, Paulus Potter's twenty-eight paintings contain it twelve times, the highest rate recorded [2]. These are computed matches to photographed, varnished paintings, not pigment identifications [2].
